summary: Scoped verification completed for logo swap + Windows installer diagnostics. Alta Pulse logos are live on login/download/authenticated sidebar, installer helper works as read-only local integrity checker, and public installer binary (0.2.1) is byte/hash consistent with release manifest and local artifact. Reported Windows launch-permission error is NOT reproduced in this Linux environment and therefore NOT confirmed fixed.

critical.issue: User-reported message 'O Windows não pode acessar o dispositivo, caminho ou arquivo especificado' could not be reproduced/validated without Windows host policy and Protection History evidence.

integration_issues.issue: Console shows repeated 401 resource errors for /api/auth/me during unauthenticated state (noise observed during automation logs).

action_items: Treat Windows launch-permission bug as unresolved until user-side Windows evidence is collected (Security > Protection History details/time-matched event).
Keep installer unchanged for now; integrity/corruption checks passed and archive is valid NSIS package.
Optional hardening: prevent unauthenticated /api/auth/me polling from surfacing as console resource errors on public pages.
critical_code_review_comments: Brand component points to /brand/alta-pulse-* assets with alt='Alta Pulse' as requested; legacy product text 'Alta Core' remains unchanged in UI copy.
installer.nsi uses per-user install scope (RequestExecutionLevel user, $LOCALAPPDATA target), consistent with non-admin installation intent.

build.mjs/installer flow contains no code-signing step; unsigned state is explicit in /api/desktop/release (signed=false) and must not be presented as proven root cause for this specific Windows message.
Public download evidence: manifest size/hash == streamed download == local release file (0.2.1, 114965344 bytes, sha256 71f3612df4fae7f0d08805e5805948369792cb4ca5c7bb50eb90e172f64c487a).
Archive integrity evidence: 7z test returned 'Everything is Ok'; extracted payload contains AltaCore.exe (PE32+ x86-64) and expected app resources.
seed_data_creation: No backend seed data created. Local temporary files only for UI checksum probe: /tmp/iter9-truncated.exe and /tmp/iter9-mutated-same-size.exe.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Scoped checks executed only for branding + installer diagnostics. Screenshots: /app/test_reports/screenshots_iter9/iter9_login_brand.jpeg, iter9_download_page.jpeg, iter9_installer_help_results.jpeg, iter9_authenticated_sidebar.jpeg. Windows execution-policy/device-access behavior still requires real Windows confirmation.
rca of the issue: RCA status: download artifact corruption/truncation not supported by evidence. Reproduction on Linux cannot emulate Windows launch policy that raises this exact message before install execution. Verified binary is intact and matches published manifest/hash; NSIS archive is extractable and payload architecture is correct (x64 app inside NSIS PE32 bootstrap). Most probable classes remain Windows-side path/access/security policy controls, but no definitive root cause can be claimed without user machine event evidence.
